card.title: Reopen the First Reason
card.instruction: Keep them present by returning to the first reason for staying and revealing that it now means something different.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't go yet. You came to return the key.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. I thought putting it down would take longer.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I needed to see whether you'd sit down before giving it up.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 returns to key handover to delay departure; A3 admits hoped-for time; A5 reveals a test of willingness to stay.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 key returned prompts A3 disappointment; B4 questions needing the key; A5 clarifies the relational purpose.

relationship.evidence: B2 completes the errand and B4 notices A's conflicting response.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4 need question to distinguish recovering an object from witnessing reluctance to leave.

specificity.evidence: A1 key return and B2 table establish completed practical business and resisted departure.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 giving it up carries emotional meaning grounded in the returned key, with quiet rather than broad wit.

coach2.missing: No essential gap: the exact key's history is unnecessary to understand the failed bid for time.
coach2.firstDefect: No mandatory defect; A5 reveals the first reason's changed meaning.

A1-B2.evidence: B2 says A1 stated errand is complete.

A3-B4.evidence: B4 asks whether A3 disappointment means the object was not needed.

B4-A5.evidence: A5 answers B4 with the hoped-for gesture of sitting down.
